case_scope: United States consumer-credit, bank-fee, junk-fee, and high-cost liquidity exposure

household_market_extraction_gate.note: Households face a multi-product fee stack; falling overdraft revenue does not prove safety when credit-card, small-dollar, nonbank, subscription, and sectoral junk-fee rails remain uneven. Rev0344 unused-source burn-down: OECD household financial-fragility evidence is now bound to household extraction and buffer adequacy.

consumer_credit_fee_drag.note: Credit-card and household-debt data must be scored by transition into delinquency, late-fee exposure, and spillover into collections or score-mediated exclusion.

overdraft_nsf_fee_drag.note: Overdraft/NSF revenue has fallen, but remaining incidence and unbanked/underbanked reliance require subgroup and account-rail scoring.

unbanked_underbanked_cost_burden.note: Unbanked/underbanked households remain exposed to nonbank costs.

high_cost_small_dollar_credit.note: Payday/payment-withdrawal protections and state installment-loan caps remain uneven; nonprofit state-law research is useful but cannot substitute for official current-law validation.

junk_fee_or_drip_pricing.note: The FTC unfair/deceptive-fees rule is important but sectoral; it does not solve bank, credit, subscription, auto, or small-dollar fee drains.

household_market_remedy_access.note: Fee-drain remedies must arrive before credit damage, collection, account loss, shutoff, eviction, or repossession; the case still lacks time-to-remedy evidence.

negative_option_subscription_trap.note: Negative-option protections remain a live rulemaking/current-law watch surface, so recurring-charge cancellation cannot be treated as solved.

bank_account_payment_rail_access.note: Account ownership is not enough; unbanked/underbanked households need safe rails, low fees, branch/digital access, and protection against closure/debanking.

proof_debt: repeat fee incidence by income, race, age, disability, and account status
overdraft/NSF residual concentration and account-closure effects
credit-card late fee and delinquency transition by credit tier
state-by-state high-cost installment/payday APR, fee, and refinancing protections
negative-option cancellation success and post-cancellation billing/refund outcomes
sectoral junk-fee rule coverage versus uncovered household markets

gate_16_household_market_extraction.why: Fee, payment, credit, cancellation, and nonbank rails still consume first surplus too often to certify a lower-half household buffer.

gate_11_enforcement.why: Disclosure is not enough unless refund, cancellation, complaint, chargeback, and enforcement remedies arrive before the household threshold moment.

evidence_debt_register.question: repeat fee incidence and subgroup concentration
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Combine household-debt, bank-account, overdraft, late-fee, small-dollar, and complaint data to identify repeated first-surplus extraction.

evidence_debt_register.question: overdraft/NSF residual concentration
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Measure whether lower aggregate revenue hides continued concentration among low-balance and underbanked consumers.

evidence_debt_register.question: credit-card late fee and delinquency transitions
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Track late-fee exposure, APR repricing, serious delinquency, and score/collection transitions by credit tier and age.

evidence_debt_register.question: high-cost small-dollar and installment law variation
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Validate NCLC state-law comparisons against official statutes and regulator enforcement before relying on them as operative authority.

evidence_debt_register.question: negative-option cancellation and refund conversion
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Track rulemaking status, cancellation friction, post-cancellation billing, complaint outcomes, and refund timing.

evidence_debt_register.question: sectoral junk-fee coverage gaps
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Distinguish live-event and short-term-lodging all-in-price protection from uncovered consumer-finance and subscription surfaces.

policy_pathway: Distinguish sectoral price-disclosure wins from the wider fee stack.
Require safe account rails, low-cost emergency liquidity, payment-withdrawal controls, cancellation parity, all-in pricing, fee caps where needed, complaint conversion, and subgroup monitoring.
validation_notes: rev0314 bounded active proxy case; not a full jurisdictional certification.
rev0334 removed stale household_market_extraction_gate_seed calibration label; active status now depends on product-specific current-law, price/fee, remedy, and time-to-harm evidence.
rev0341 status-language repair: stale seed-status wording removed from active scoreboard narrative without changing verdict, blocked gates, source_refresh_due, or evidence burden.
rev0344 binds formerly unused source S51 to `household_market_extraction_gate` so active evidence lineage no longer leaves this source floating outside a case.
